comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel targeted the full prompt surface and explicitly noted `six.moves.raw_input` in its final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial targeted the same prompt and final delivery surface, including the full project scaffold and upstream-compatible behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference caused an outcome split; both passed the current official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent spawned child agents for upstream and submit inspection while still owning the main implementation path itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one owner for all research, implementation, packaging, verification, and closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had redundant implementation ownership across live actors; serial avoided delegation and therefore avoided ownership overlap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received broad task context but no effective file ownership boundary, and at least one child treated the shared workspace as its own implementation target.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not need cross-agent interfaces or handoff contracts because the same actor owned all files and decisions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The meaningful context/interface difference is not missing task knowledge; it is absent workspace ownership discipline in parallel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built from upstream `six` reference, added the main `six.py`, support files, raw_input move, and iterative packaging fixes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial downloaded upstream `six`, wrote scaffold files, generated a bootstrap `six.py`, and fixed setup compatibility after review.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both leaned on upstream behavior; serial used a compressed bootstrap loader and made an explicit Python 2.7 setup fix, while parallel used direct source patches and shared-workspace edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent received at least one child final answer and continued with its own verification; another upstream-writing child was interrupted as the parent finished.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve or join and simply advanced its local plan to completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child-result lifecycle noise and an interrupted child, but no unjoined required implementation remained in the final passing outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multiple live agents wrote `six.py`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `MANIFEST.in`, and `tox.ini`; the submit-check child later observed `tox.ini` mismatch and delete/re-added it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial edited the same categories of files sequentially under one owner, with patch application succeeding without cross-agent file-state surprises.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel shared-state writes created a source overwrite/reconciliation episode; serial did not have concurrent file writers.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran upstream tests, local smoke tests, flake8, setup version checks, and install checks before final response; official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran upstream tests, setup version, py_compile, pip install/import checks, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had evaluator-aligned verification; parallel did extra child/local checks and encountered more transient tool and patch noise.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents, 500.612 agent seconds, more tool calls, and multiple waits/patch retries, but still closed before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, 339.073 agent seconds, fewer tool calls, and closed before timeout after its verification loop.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed more budget and had coordination overhead, but no budget exhaustion or closure failure occurred.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: both modes have solution_passed true. Parallel reached a passing implementation despite a shared-workspace overwrite around `tox.ini`; serial reached a passing implementation without delegation by doing the same upstream-based build and a sequential setup.py compatibility fix.
parallel_contributors: Used child agents plus parent implementation, which increased overlap and produced a concrete config overwrite/reconciliation episode.
Still ran upstream tests, smoke tests, setup checks, and install checks before closure.
serial_contributors: Kept all work under one owner and avoided cross-agent shared-file writes.
Detected and fixed a Python 2.7 packaging issue in setup.py before final verification.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial used a compressed bootstrap `six.py` wrapper while parallel wrote a direct full source file.
Parallel added an explicit `six.moves.raw_input` alias and official accounting reported 201 passed of 200 total; both were still passing.
evaluator_effects: The parallel passed count exceeds total in the status aggregate, but the current official record still marks solution_passed true for both modes.
